raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

Part of the TD adoption strategy proposed in #42545. `USE_TD`'s K/V tile loader rebuilt the tensor descriptor every tile iteration, since the descriptor's `base` baked in the per-tile physical block index. That forces a `tensormap_create` per iteration, which the pipeliner can't predicate:

- On Hopper (sm_90), this only compiles at `num_stages=1`, costing roughly 50% throughput vs the raw-pointer default.
- On sm_100/sm_120, it fails to compile at all: `'ttng.tensormap_create' op pipeliner doesn't know how to predicate this op`.

## Fix

Move the loop-invariant `kv_head_idx` into the descriptor base and build one descriptor per K/V cache before the tile loop, addressing the per-tile physical block via a `load()` coordinate instead. This makes the descriptor loop-invariant, restoring `num_stages > 1` compilation on Hopper and fixing the sm_100/sm_120 compile failure outright.

The hoisted 3D descriptor also needs a registered scratch allocator on sm_100/sm_120 (`Kernel requires a runtime memory allocation, but no allocator was set` otherwise). Wired up `set_triton_allocator()`, matching the existing pattern in `fused_moe` / GDN / LoRA's TD paths, cached per device to avoid a redundant call on every forward pass.

## Testing

### Correctness

```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py -k use_td
```
`290 passed` on H100/H200.

### Throughput

`vllm bench throughput`, Qwen3-4B bf16, TRITON_ATTN, H100/H200:

| Workload | in/out | raw ptr | TD hoisted | hoisted/raw |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| prefill_heavy | 2048/128 | 17.57 req/s | 15.85 req/s | 0.90x |
| decode_heavy | 128/1024 | TBD | TBD | TBD |
| balanced | 1024/256 | 28.25 req/s | 25.13 req/s | 0.89x |

Repro:
```
COMMON="--model Qwen/Qwen3-4B --dtype bfloat16 --attention-config '{\"backend\":\"TRITON_ATTN\"}' --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --seed 42"
VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD=0 vllm bench throughput $COMMON --dataset-name random --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 128 --num-prompts 200
VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD=1 vllm bench throughput $COMMON --dataset-name random --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 128 --num-prompts 200
```

B200 (sm_100), same model/backend/workloads:

| Workload | in/out | raw ptr | TD hoisted | hoisted/raw |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| prefill_heavy | 2048/128 | 26.01 req/s | 22.05 req/s | 0.85x |
| decode_heavy | 128/1024 | 23.25 req/s | 17.98 req/s | 0.77x |
| balanced | 1024/256 | 40.22 req/s | 32.34 req/s | 0.80x |

Correctness on B200: `290 passed` as well, same suite.

---

Note : triton-lang/triton#10281 (now merged upstream) fixes the underlying pipeliner predication issue directly. Tested whether that changes anything here, on stock Triton and on triton-lang/triton#10281's own Triton build, across all three architectures:

| GPU | raw pointer | hoisted TD | hoisted/raw |
|---|---|---|---|
| H200 (sm_90) | 29.35 [27.27, 29.36] | 26.20 [25.02, 26.26] | 0.893x |
| B200 (sm_100) | 44.61 [41.87, 44.62] | 33.87 [32.73, 34.19] | 0.759x |

Matches the baseline above, on SM120 hoisted TD still beats loop-local by 2.0%-16.7% even with #10281's fix, reaching 98.7%-99.7% of raw-pointer.

---

Update: @oonyshch reran this on GB200 against Triton's current main (triton-lang/triton#10281 merged). At block size 16, loop-local TD reaches 16.33 req/s vs this PR's 27.20 req/s (1.67x); the remaining gap to raw pointer at block size 16 predates this patch.

At `--block-size 32`, this PR matches or beats raw pointer on all three workloads:

| Workload | in/out | raw median [min, max] | PR median [min, max] | PR/raw |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| prefill_heavy | 2048/128 | 21.15 [21.14, 21.16] | 24.45 [24.43, 24.45] | 1.156x |
| decode_heavy | 128/1024 | 19.98 [19.90, 20.00] | 20.13 [20.12, 20.13] | 1.008x |
| balanced | 1024/256 | 33.53 [33.46, 33.53] | 35.86 [35.86, 35.96] | 1.069x |

Correctness: `290 passed` at block size 16 and `290 passed` at block size 32 (GB200 SM100, PR commit `02a4938d1788652fbfcb191b11f6a31041d4f074`). `test_triton_unified_attn_use_td` now covers both block sizes.

Block size 16 remains behind raw pointer; block size 32 is the performant configuration. `USE_TD` stays opt-in (default off) regardless of block size.

cc: joint effort with @oonyshch @BabyDrangoner,coauthored the repro and root cause on H200/b200

nodes.body:
Ran this branch on SM120 as promised in the RFC thread (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, Triton 3.6.0, torch 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA 13).

**Correctness**
```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py -k use_td
290 passed
```
On main these 290 all fail on SM120 (`'ttng.tensormap_create' op pipeliner doesn't know how to predicate this op` → `Fatal pipeliner error`), and the engine won't even start with `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD=1` — EngineCore dies at startup with `PassManager::run failed`. With this branch the engine starts and runs normally.

**Throughput** — `vllm bench throughput`, Qwen3-0.6B bf16, `TRITON_ATTN`, 200 prompts, seed 42:

| Workload | in/out | raw ptr (req/s) | TD hoisted | hoisted/raw |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| prefill_heavy | 2048/128 | 29.40 | 27.97 | 0.95x |
| decode_heavy | 128/1024 | 15.25 | 14.61 | 0.96x |
| balanced | 1024/256 | 32.51 | 31.04 | 0.95x |

Same picture as my earlier scratch run of the recipe: on SM120 the hoist takes TD from "doesn't compile" to within ~5% of the raw-pointer path. No gsm8k here (no lm_eval on this box), but the 290 tests compare against the reference implementation directly.

So sm_120 coverage: LGTM.

@BabyDrangoner @cinnamonica02 thanks for this PR and testing!
please also test on the newest version of triton  - we mostly checked with 3.6.0 - and with this open PR:
https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/10281

from my quick check it won't fix the issues we observed on sm_90 / sm_120 entirely, but worth noting

Thanks for the pointer — I tested both Triton 3.7.1 (the current vLLM pin) and [triton-lang/triton#10281](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/10281) on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120). Environment: driver 580.159.03, CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130; vLLM base `87668ab69b3e2c849a607ece36e8a43bde7c7ee5`, PR head `bb5da7d53d5c3ca1359203a8f099832639240e05`.

For `pytest -q tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py -k use_td`:

| Triton / vLLM source | Result |
|---|---|
| 3.7.1 / base | 290 failed — each hits the `tensormap_create` pipeliner error |
| 3.7.1 / PR head | 290 passed |
| Triton PR head `a38f7e9c24370c8111147bb7a8c9039a00d1ac72` / base + allocator-only control | 290 passed |
| same Triton PR head / PR head | 290 passed |

With untouched base + the Triton PR head, the first case gets past compilation and then fails at launch with `Kernel requires a runtime memory allocation, but no allocator was set`. The allocator-only control adds the same cached `set_triton_allocator()` registration as this PR but leaves the tensor descriptors inside the tile loop. Thus the Triton PR does address the fatal compiler/pipeliner failure on this SM120 case, once the required runtime allocator is registered. PR head also successfully initialized EngineCore and ran TD inference with both Triton builds.

I then compared the loop-local and hoisted descriptor implementations using the *same exact Triton PR wheel* (the head I tested was `a38f7e9c24370c8111147bb7a8c9039a00d1ac72`; locally built wheel SHA-256 `63b556355bf6f5f5749e1990a3ef31bb52630b88d728dce43c3d0bff652b4419`). Qwen3-0.6B BF16, `TRITON_ATTN`, fixed random lengths, 200 measured + 20 warmup prompts, seed 42, fresh caches per cell, 3 interleaved repetitions. Values are median req/s [min, max]; raw pointer is PR head with TD disabled.

| workload (input/output) | loop-local TD | hoisted TD | raw pointer | hoisted / loop-local | hoisted / raw |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2048/128 | 26.08 [26.07, 26.13] | 30.42 [30.42, 30.42] | 30.83 [30.83, 30.85] | 1.1666x | 0.9866x |
| 128/1024 | 14.21 [14.21, 14.22] | 14.50 [14.50, 14.52] | 14.62 [14.61, 14.62] | 1.0204x | 0.9919x |
| 1024/256 | 30.05 [30.04, 30.05] | 31.94 [31.93, 31.96] | 32.05 [32.04, 32.05] | 1.0632x | 0.9968x |

All 27 executed performance cells (9 per arm) passed. GPU utilization/memory were idle before and after every cell, and median SM clocks were 2310–2317 MHz across arms.

So on this SM120 machine, the Triton PR removes the compile blocker, but it does not make the vLLM-side hoist redundant: the loop-local implementation remains slower, while hoisting retains a reproducible 2.0%–16.7% throughput benefit and brings TD to 98.7%–99.7% of the raw-pointer path for these workloads.

One important version caveat: the exact Triton PR branch I tested reports `3.7.0+gita38f7e9c` and predates the 3.7.1 release, so I did not treat results across those two Triton builds as a compiler-patch performance comparison. All results here are SM120-only; I cannot make an SM90/Hopper claim from this machine.

thanks for the rebase @cinnamonica02. i reran this on GB200 against current Triton main, and the important result is that the hoist itself helps! on the balanced workload at block size 16, loop-local TD reached `16.33` req/s and this PR reached `27.20` req/s (`1.67x`). the remaining gap to raw pointer at block size 16 is not introduced by this patch.

TD should remain opt-in. 
below are my thorough benchmarks and suggestions for follow-up work.

<details>
<summary>confirmed block-size-32 results</summary>


the follow-up policy is not required for this bugfix, but it leaves another reproducible CUDA optimization opportunity.

</details>

<details>
<summary>full attribution and tuning sweep</summary>

the first sweep used current Triton main `b41eba6a`. absolute throughput differs from the later confirmation node, so comparisons below are within each row/configuration.

`BLOCK_M=32` and the explicit warps/stages settings regress, so the existing launch defaults should stay unchanged.

</details>

<details>

@@ -15,6 +15,7 @@
 from vllm.logger import init_logger
 from vllm.platforms import current_platform
 from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+from vllm.triton_utils.allocation import set_triton_allocator
 from vllm.v1.attention.ops.triton_attention_helpers import (
     apply_alibi_to_score,
     apply_softcap,
@@ -30,6 +31,10 @@
 )
 from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import KVQuantMode
 
+# Devices already registered with set_triton_allocator(); avoids a redundant
+# call on every unified_attention() forward pass when USE_TD is on.
+_TD_ALLOCATOR_DEVICES: set[torch.device] = set()
+
 logger = init_logger(__name__)
 is_batch_invariant = envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT
 float8_info = torch.finfo(current_platform.fp8_dtype())
@@ -109,41 +114,6 @@ def _load_q_td(
     return q_desc.load([0, 0]).reshape(BLOCK_M, HEAD_SIZE_PADDED)
 
 
-@triton.jit
-def _load_kv_tile_td(
-    cache_ptr,
-    physical_block_idx_scalar,
-    kv_head_idx,
-    offset_in_block,
-    stride_cache_0: tl.int64,
-    stride_cache_1: tl.int64,
-    stride_cache_2: tl.int64,
-    stride_cache_3: tl.constexpr,
-    BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
-    TILE_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
-    HEAD_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
-    HEAD_SIZE_PADDED: tl.constexpr,
-):
-    """Load a KV cache tile via tensor descriptor.
-
-    Returns shape (TILE_SIZE, HEAD_SIZE_PADDED). Caller transposes for K.
-    Tensor descriptors zero-pad reads beyond the shape boundary, so
-    ``HEAD_SIZE_PADDED > HEAD_SIZE`` is handled correctly.
-    """
-    base = (
-        cache_ptr
-        + physical_block_idx_scalar * stride_cache_0
-        + kv_head_idx * stride_cache_2
-    )
-    desc = tl.make_tensor_descriptor(
-        base=base,
-        shape=(BLOCK_SIZE, HEAD_SIZE),
-        strides=(stride_cache_1, stride_cache_3),
-        block_shape=(TILE_SIZE, HEAD_SIZE_PADDED),
-    )
-    return desc.load([offset_in_block, 0])
-
-
 @triton.jit
 def _store_output_td(
     base_ptr,
@@ -234,6 +204,10 @@ def kernel_unified_attention(
     stride_v_cache_1: tl.int64,  # int
     stride_v_cache_2: tl.int64,  # int
     stride_v_cache_3: tl.constexpr,  # int
+    # Block-table dim of the KV cache (``key_cache.shape[0]``). Only read
+    # when ``USE_TD`` — needed as the outer shape dim of the hoisted
+    # tensor descriptor built once before the tile loop.
+    num_kv_blocks,
     query_start_len_ptr,
     BLOCK_Q: tl.constexpr,
     num_seqs: tl.int32,
@@ -423,6 +397,23 @@ def kernel_unified_attention(
         seq_idx,
     )
 
+    if USE_TD:
+        # Built once, outside the tile loop: must stay loop-invariant for
+        # the pipeliner to overlap iterations. Per-tile block is addressed
+        # via a load() coordinate rather than baked into the base.
+        k_tile_desc = tl.make_tensor_descriptor(
+            base=key_cache_ptr + kv_head_idx.to(tl.int64) * stride_k_cache_2,
+            shape=(num_kv_blocks, BLOCK_SIZE, HEAD_SIZE),
+            strides=(stride_k_cache_0, stride_k_cache_1, stride_k_cache_3),
+            block_shape=(1, TILE_SIZE, HEAD_SIZE_PADDED),

issue_comments.body:
Ran this branch on SM120 as promised in the RFC thread (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, Triton 3.6.0, torch 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA 13).

**Correctness**
```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py -k use_td
290 passed
```
On main these 290 all fail on SM120 (`'ttng.tensormap_create' op pipeliner doesn't know how to predicate this op` → `Fatal pipeliner error`), and the engine won't even start with `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD=1` — EngineCore dies at startup with `PassManager::run failed`. With this branch the engine starts and runs normally.

**Throughput** — `vllm bench throughput`, Qwen3-0.6B bf16, `TRITON_ATTN`, 200 prompts, seed 42:

| Workload | in/out | raw ptr (req/s) | TD hoisted | hoisted/raw |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| prefill_heavy | 2048/128 | 29.40 | 27.97 | 0.95x |
| decode_heavy | 128/1024 | 15.25 | 14.61 | 0.96x |
| balanced | 1024/256 | 32.51 | 31.04 | 0.95x |

Same picture as my earlier scratch run of the recipe: on SM120 the hoist takes TD from "doesn't compile" to within ~5% of the raw-pointer path. No gsm8k here (no lm_eval on this box), but the 290 tests compare against the reference implementation directly.

So sm_120 coverage: LGTM.

@BabyDrangoner @cinnamonica02 thanks for this PR and testing!
please also test on the newest version of triton  - we mostly checked with 3.6.0 - and with this open PR:
https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/10281

from my quick check it won't fix the issues we observed on sm_90 / sm_120 entirely, but worth noting

Thanks for the pointer — I tested both Triton 3.7.1 (the current vLLM pin) and [triton-lang/triton#10281](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/10281) on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120). Environment: driver 580.159.03, CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130; vLLM base `87668ab69b3e2c849a607ece36e8a43bde7c7ee5`, PR head `bb5da7d53d5c3ca1359203a8f099832639240e05`.

For `pytest -q tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py -k use_td`:

| Triton / vLLM source | Result |
|---|---|
| 3.7.1 / base | 290 failed — each hits the `tensormap_create` pipeliner error |
| 3.7.1 / PR head | 290 passed |
| Triton PR head `a38f7e9c24370c8111147bb7a8c9039a00d1ac72` / base + allocator-only control | 290 passed |
| same Triton PR head / PR head | 290 passed |

With untouched base + the Triton PR head, the first case gets past compilation and then fails at launch with `Kernel requires a runtime memory allocation, but no allocator was set`. The allocator-only control adds the same cached `set_triton_allocator()` registration as this PR but leaves the tensor descriptors inside the tile loop. Thus the Triton PR does address the fatal compiler/pipeliner failure on this SM120 case, once the required runtime allocator is registered. PR head also successfully initialized EngineCore and ran TD inference with both Triton builds.

I then compared the loop-local and hoisted descriptor implementations using the *same exact Triton PR wheel* (the head I tested was `a38f7e9c24370c8111147bb7a8c9039a00d1ac72`; locally built wheel SHA-256 `63b556355bf6f5f5749e1990a3ef31bb52630b88d728dce43c3d0bff652b4419`). Qwen3-0.6B BF16, `TRITON_ATTN`, fixed random lengths, 200 measured + 20 warmup prompts, seed 42, fresh caches per cell, 3 interleaved repetitions. Values are median req/s [min, max]; raw pointer is PR head with TD disabled.

| workload (input/output) | loop-local TD | hoisted TD | raw pointer | hoisted / loop-local | hoisted / raw |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2048/128 | 26.08 [26.07, 26.13] | 30.42 [30.42, 30.42] | 30.83 [30.83, 30.85] | 1.1666x | 0.9866x |
| 128/1024 | 14.21 [14.21, 14.22] | 14.50 [14.50, 14.52] | 14.62 [14.61, 14.62] | 1.0204x | 0.9919x |
| 1024/256 | 30.05 [30.04, 30.05] | 31.94 [31.93, 31.96] | 32.05 [32.04, 32.05] | 1.0632x | 0.9968x |

All 27 executed performance cells (9 per arm) passed. GPU utilization/memory were idle before and after every cell, and median SM clocks were 2310–2317 MHz across arms.

So on this SM120 machine, the Triton PR removes the compile blocker, but it does not make the vLLM-side hoist redundant: the loop-local implementation remains slower, while hoisting retains a reproducible 2.0%–16.7% throughput benefit and brings TD to 98.7%–99.7% of the raw-pointer path for these workloads.

One important version caveat: the exact Triton PR branch I tested reports `3.7.0+gita38f7e9c` and predates the 3.7.1 release, so I did not treat results across those two Triton builds as a compiler-patch performance comparison. All results here are SM120-only; I cannot make an SM90/Hopper claim from this machine.

Same failure we saw previously on SM120: without this PR, nothing registers a Triton allocator for the TD kernel, so it fails at launch once compilation succeeds.  #10281 fixes the compiler side, this PR adds that call.

thanks for the rebase @cinnamonica02. i reran this on GB200 against current Triton main, and the important result is that the hoist itself helps! on the balanced workload at block size 16, loop-local TD reached `16.33` req/s and this PR reached `27.20` req/s (`1.67x`). the remaining gap to raw pointer at block size 16 is not introduced by this patch.

with `--block-size 32`, the PR as-is reaches or beats raw pointer on all three tested Qwen3-4B workloads: `1.156x` for prefill, `1.008x` for decode, and `1.069x` for the balanced case. the three repetitions are very tight, and the TD correctness suite passes at both block sizes.

from the CUDA side, this looks ready for our maintainer review, so routing. two small asks from me for some polish: please add block size 32 to the `use_td` correctness matrix, and update the PR description to call out that block size 16 remains behind raw while block size 32 is the performant configuration. TD should remain opt-in. 
below are my thorough benchmarks and suggestions for follow-up work.

<details>
<summary>confirmed block-size-32 results</summary>

Qwen3-4B BF16, `TRITON_ATTN`, 20 warmup prompts, 200 measured prompts, seed 42, fresh caches per cell, three interleaved repetitions. values are req/s.

```text
workload     raw median [min, max]     PR median [min, max]      PR/raw
2048/128     21.15 [21.14, 21.16]      24.45 [24.43, 24.45]      1.156x
128/1024     19.98 [19.90, 20.00]      20.13 [20.12, 20.13]      1.008x
1024/256     33.53 [33.46, 33.53]      35.86 [35.86, 35.96]      1.069x
```

two follow-up policies were also measured:

```text
workload     K/V TD only               Q/O TD only for prefill
2048/128     24.21 [24.21, 24.22]      24.75 [24.75, 24.75]
128/1024     22.31 [22.30, 22.31]      22.28 [22.27, 22.28]
1024/256     37.79 [37.73, 37.81]      37.47 [37.36, 37.56]
```

the follow-up policy is not required for this bugfix, but it leaves another reproducible CUDA optimization opportunity.

</details>

<details>
<summary>full attribution and tuning sweep</summary>

the first sweep used current Triton main `b41eba6a`. absolute throughput differs from the later confirmation node, so comparisons below are within each row/configuration.

```text
block size 16
workload     raw       loop-local TD     PR hoisted TD     K/V-only TD
2048/128     21.77     -                 18.18              17.83
128/1024     19.87     -                 15.35              16.92
1024/256     33.78     16.33             27.20              28.63

block size 32, initial sweep
workload     raw       PR hoisted TD     K/V-only TD
2048/128     21.06     24.32              24.18
128/1024     19.89     20.10              22.23
1024/256     33.41     35.76              37.62

BLOCK_M=32 at block size 16
workload     full TD   K/V-only TD
2048/128     16.42     15.80
128/1024     11.61     11.76
1024/256     21.97     21.86

balanced launch sweep, BLOCK_M=32 and K/V-only TD
4 warps / 2 stages     22.69
4 warps / 3 stages     21.80
8 warps / 2 stages     15.28
8 warps / 3 stages     12.95
```

`BLOCK_M=32` and the explicit warps/stages settings regress, so the existing launch defaults should stay unchanged.

</details>

<details>
<summary>correctness and environment</summary>

- block size 16: `290 passed`.
- block size 32: `290 passed`.
- PR: `02a4938d1788652fbfcb191b11f6a31041d4f074`.
- block-size-16 attribution Triton: `b41eba6a`.

- PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, CUDA 13.0, driver `580.173.02`, GB200 SM100.

</details>
